title: Reverse currying for one pair of module sheaves
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. For $R$-module sheaves $S,A,B,D$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], a morphism $f:S\to\mathcal Hom_R(A\otimes_R B,D)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] admits a morphism $b:S\to\mathcal Hom_R(A,\mathcal Hom_R(B,D))$. For $s$ over $U$, $W\to U$, $x\in A(W)$ and $y\in B(W)$, evaluating $f_U(s)_W$ on the presheaf-to-sheaf tensor image of $x\otimes y$ equals evaluating $b_U(s)_W(x)$ on $y$ at the identity localization over $W$. The tensor image is the map of [def-sc-hom-tensor-degreewise-equation].

proof.text: Reuse the separate-universe presheaf currying and uncurrying constructions already proved privately in HomTensorPair, loaded by a proof-only import all. Precompose the tensor map with the presheaf-to-sheaf tensor map. Uncurry the source parameter S by evaluation at the identity localization, reorder B, A, S using presheaf braiding and associativity, and curry twice. The existing additivity, scalar compatibility, restriction compatibility and evaluation lemmas supply these constructions without restating or proving them again.

Evaluate the two curried maps at x and y. The identity restriction of the pair x tensor the restriction of s is the same pair. Naturality of f identifies evaluation at the identity slice after restriction with evaluation at W. This gives the displayed equality.

theorem homTensorReversePair_construct (S A B D : Mod) :
    letI := monoidalCategory R
    ∀ f : S ⟶ homObj (R := R) (A ⊗ B) D,
    ∃ b : S ⟶ homObj (R := R) A (homObj (R := R) B D),
      ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (s : S.val.obj U) (W : (Over U.unop)ᵒᵖ)
        (x : A.val.obj (op W.unop.left)) (y : B.val.obj (op W.unop.left)),
        (((f.val.app U).hom s).app W).hom
          (((CategoryTheory.homTensorCurrySectionMap R A B).app
            (op W.unop.left)).hom (x ⊗ₜ[R.obj.obj (op W.unop.left)] y)) =
        (((((b.val.app U).hom s).app W).hom x).app
          (op (Over.mk (𝟙 W.unop.left)))).hom y
